rejected_rule.statement: The subject matter jurisdiction of the Commercial High Court is established where the debt, damage or demand set out in the plaint exceeds the amount as may be fixed by the Minister from time to time, by Notification published in the Gazette.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: The three words ‘debt’, ‘damage’ or ‘demand’ in Item (1) of the First Schedule to the Act must be interpreted in an ejusdem generis manner. I prefer to establish jurisdiction of the Commercial High Court on the sum claimed in the plaint as debt, damage or demand, and thereby bring certainty, rather than waste the time and resources of litigants and Court by establishing jurisdiction on the sum awarded in the judgment which may lead to the dismissal of the action merely because the sum finally awarded is lower than the amount prescribed by the Minister.
rejected_rule.statute_citation_verbatim: Section 2(1) of the High Court of the Provinces (Special Provisions) Act No. 10 of 1996 (Act)
